Match on the time-conditional propensity score

Source: R/Matching.R
matchOnTcps.Rd

Performs greedy nearest-neighbour matching of switchers to comparators within each exposure set using the `propensityScore` column produced by [fitTcps()]. Unmatched persons are dropped. Returns the matched population with a new `stratumId` column that identifies each matched set (used as the stratum in outcome models).

Usage

matchOnTcps(population, matchingArgs)

Arguments

population

A data frame (typically `dplyr::collect(pnuData$studyPopulation)`) with a `propensityScore` column added by [fitTcps()]. Must contain `row_id`, `treatment`, `exposure_set_id`, and `propensityScore`.

matchingArgs

A `MatchingArgs` object from [createMatchingArgs()].

Value

`population` filtered to matched persons and with an additional integer `stratumId` column. Each stratum contains exactly one switcher and one to `maxRatio` comparators (or all within-caliper comparators when `maxRatio = 0`).

Details

The caliper is computed once across all exposure sets. When `caliperScale = "standardized logit"` (default), the caliper width is `caliper * SD(logit(PS))` pooled across the full population. This mirrors CohortMethod's behaviour.

Within each exposure set, cases (switchers, `treatment = 1`) are processed in ascending PS order. For each case, all available comparators within the caliper are identified; the nearest (up to `maxRatio`) are selected and assigned the same stratum ID. Stratum IDs are unique integers across the whole returned population.

References

Suissa S, Moodie EE, Dell'Aniello S. Prevalent new-user cohort designs for comparative drug effect studies by time-conditional propensity scores. *Pharmacoepidemiol Drug Saf* 2017;26(4):459-468. doi:10.1002/pds.4117

See also

[createMatchingArgs()], [fitTcps()]

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
simArgs <- createSimulationArgs(nSwitchers = 500L, nCovariates = 5L, seed = 1L)
pnuData <- simulatePnuData(simArgs)
spArgs <- createStudyPopulationArgs(outcomeId = 1L)
pnuData <- createStudyPopulation(pnuData, spArgs)
pop <- dplyr::collect(pnuData$studyPopulation)
tcpsArgs <- createTcpsArgs(
  prior   = Cyclops::createPrior("normal", variance = 0.1),
  control = Cyclops::createControl(noiseLevel = "silent")
)
pop <- fitTcps(pop, pnuData, tcpsArgs)
matchingArgs <- createMatchingArgs(caliper = 0.2, maxRatio = 1L)
matched <- matchOnTcps(pop, matchingArgs)
Andromeda::close(pnuData)
} # }
